executiveSummary: Immediate Priority: Confirmed GNSS spoofing/jamming continues to affect vessel approaches and transits in key Middle East corridors, and a surge in AIS deception incidents in the Indo-Pacific is degrading maritime situational awareness. Port OT risk remains elevated under MARAD Advisory 2026-007. Confidence: medium-to-high. Available reporting indicates multiple concurrent maritime cyber-relevant pressures this period. Confirmed GPS/GNSS interference impacting vessels near Fujairah and Oman presents direct navigation risk to bridge operations and ECDIS integrity. View Article Vessel-reported GNSS spoofing/jamming in the Red Sea remains an active concern per USCG NAVCEN inputs. Government Advisory Current reporting suggests identity-deception activity using AIS falsification has surged, with 40 incidents recorded in June across the IFC's area of responsibility. This activity may increase risk to traffic monitoring, screening, and voyage risk assessment. View Article The collected intelligence supports an assessment that ports and terminals should treat supply-chain and OT exposure as elevated due to the ongoing MARAD 2026-007 advisory, which highlights risks associated with PRC-manufactured cranes, Nuctech equipment, and LOGINK logistics platforms and provides explicit segmentation and monitoring guidance. Government Advisory Separately, an updated U.S. government alert summarized by industry media warns of Iranian actors targeting ICS equipment (Siemens, Schneider, Rockwell) via access to PLC ecosystems with capabilities including logic modification and disabling alarms; while not maritime-specific, these TTPs are applicable to port and offshore OT if exposed. Supporting Report Facts reported: Confirmed GNSS interference near Fujairah/Oman and Red Sea; 40 AIS-deception incidents in June; active MARAD 2026-007 advisory; ICS-targeting alert by U.S. agencies. Analytical assessment: Navigation assurance and vessel identification are the most immediate operational concerns; port OT cyber exposure requires near-term segmentation and vendor-access review. Outlook judgment: Over the next 72 hours, continued AIS deception and intermittent GNSS interference are likely in affected waterways; advisory-driven hardening steps at ports/terminals may accelerate. Confidence: medium.
